scope: Repeated save requests retain at most one active worker and one pending-capture bit per connection, rather than one queued worker per request.
Each admitted capture takes the existing account lock, rechecks current connection ownership and captures fresh canonical state; no detached stale snapshot queue.
Request coordination never holds its mutex during character/world locking or journal/database IO. Other accounts remain independent.
Existing durable journal, retry behavior and independent final shutdown save remain authoritative. Sealed admission preserves pending state and signals failure instead of pretending to save.
Earned-completion jobs and their reward journals are unchanged.

evidence: Eight concurrent producers issue 512 requests during a blocked commit; a fresh second capture and a late third mutation produce exactly three distinct receipts, retaining latest Gold, XP, health, mana and equipped item.
A blocked account does not block a different account's save.
A replaced/retired connection cannot save over the replacement owner.
Failed commits retain the latest actual disk journal, and retry commits that latest state.
Closed work admission creates no worker or fake successful commit; the independent final save persists the latest state.
Existing character persistence, account-work serialization, stale cleanup and late-reward shutdown regression tests also pass.
checks.fixture: Actual disposable disk journal with injected commit barriers/failures; no Mongo, production account or network mutation.

limits: Per-connection save coalescing does not bound all persistence, cleanup or earned-completion work across repeated connections. It does not close the complete worker-admission gate or certify 100-player capacity.
A pending-capture bit is not a durability acknowledgement. Existing journal/database errors remain failed saves, with recovery handled by the retained journal/retry/final-save paths.
The earlier afed008d connected-account binary check predates this change and is not relabeled as latest-source coverage.
No 1.72 version promotion, CI publication or public acceptance is claimed.
